note: One-off probe output (deleted after the run). Presses the real skill button on the `frostlord` form under two loadouts that differ ONLY in which owned skill the button releases, then reads `damageBy`. The two arms differ in nothing else, so the field's own damage is the same quantity in both and the difference is the release.

findings.mergeNotLoss: The release did not vanish: `G2_FROST_E` reads 152.924308992 in the safe arm and 1136.009152512 in the hazard arm - ratio 7.4286. The extra is the release, whose `boost` (6, `manualTrack.json`) rides on the field's own key because `hit`/`hitBoss` rename the source to `${source}_E` while `manualCast` is set.
findings.whyTheSafeArmStillReleases: `action('skill')` on the evolution journey runs `journeyCombat.action('skill')` and then `releaseManual()` unconditionally (`CombatSimulation:270-273`), so the button releases whatever `manualSkill()` names - the loadout, not the filter, is what keeps `A011_E` the landing key.
findings.isThisLiveToday: No. All four pressure cells call `make(spec, rank)` with no skills, so `manualSkill()` is `undefined` and nothing can be released. The hazard is latent, and it is exactly one loadout edit away (`{G2_FROST: 1}`, or `{A011: 1, G2_FROST: 3}`).
